messages:
support-escalations: hey @eng-sre — getting multiple customer tickets about huge p99 spikes from eu-west for hosted /v1/generate over the last ~18m. p50 stable, p95 up to ~620ms, p99 jumping to ~4.8s. linking a couple traces: https://redwood-traces/internal/trace/abc123 and synthetic probe results. Any immediate triage? :eyes:

ben.sre: saw the alert group, looking now. do we have affected customer IPs or client probe IDs?

support-escalations: attaching quick synthetic probe (from our eu-probe-1):
```
traceroute to api.redwood.ai (34.223.10.9), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.1.0.1  0.34 ms  0.27 ms  0.24 ms
 2  100.64.3.2  1.12 ms  0.98 ms  1.01 ms
 3  35.182.44.2  12.8 ms  13.1 ms  12.9 ms
 4  52.17.90.5  128.7 ms  129.1 ms  128.8 ms  <-- large jump
 5  34.223.10.9  130.2 ms  129.7 ms  130.0 ms
```
SYN retransmits also visible in tcpdump around the same windows (counts spiking).

maria.net: whoa that hop at 52.17.90.5 looks like a different AZ/peering plane. I'm pulling GSLB weights and recent DNS publishes now. anyone touch DNS/GSLB in last hour?

ashley.prod: i deployed an emergency routing tweak ~25m ago to shift weight off eu-pop-1 because of a CPU issue. i set eu-pop-3 weight higher as temporary. TTL stayed at 30s but we pushed the change twice. no DNS zone edit but internal GSLB publish happened.

ben.sre: confirmed timeline aligns. probe spike starts ~6m after the first publish. check shows increased cross-az RTTs and a cluster of connections that are being hairpinned through a peering transit in eu-pop-3. looks like some clients kept affinity to old backend and ended up with a circuitous route.

oncall-bot: alert: p99_latency /v1/generate (eu-west) > 2500 ms — threshold breach at 5043216900.

maria.net: digging into edge proxy logs — connection establishment times look fine on the local POP, but the origin handshake (upstream to serving region) is showing extra 120-250ms per request for certain source ASNs. also seeing higher TCP retransmit rate ~0.8% vs baseline 0.05%.

support-escalations: customers asking for ETA. can we mitigate quickly?

ben.sre: short mitigations: 1) revert GSLB weight change to previous steady-state, 2) drain eu-pop-3 from new sessions, 3) enable route affinity override for hosted traffic to prefer eu-pop-1/2 for 15m. i'll kick the controlplane steps now.

maria.net: also lowering GSLB publish frequency (ttl back to 60s) and bumping health-check sensitivity so we avoid flip-flopping while the cpu issue is resolved.

ben.sre: running drain for eu-pop-3:
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pops/eu-pop-3/drain" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" -d '{"mode":"graceful","timeout_s":600}'
```
started at 5043217120. routing override pushed at 5043217150 (forced affinities -> eu-pop-1/2).

ashley.prod: rolling back the weight bump now and pausing my autoscaler job that touched the CPU. will follow up with a proper fix for the cpu hotloop.

oncall-bot: info: drain job (eu-pop-3) status -> draining (sessions: 432 -> 120).

ben.sre: initial signs look good — p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~950ms within one minute of override. still above baseline but improving. continuing to watch for retransmit rate and SYN backoff.

maria.net: recommending a temporary traffic-steer policy: pin 80% of traffic to eu-pop-1/2 and keep 20% to eu-pop-3 for slow drain. also open a ticket to network to examine peering route via transit 52.17.90.5 — that path is adding ~120ms when used.

support-escalations: relaying to customers: "we've isolated a routing change that caused a subset of requests to traverse a longer peering path; we reverted the change and are draining the affected POP — latency is improving and we'll keep you updated."

ben.sre: action items assigned: maria to investigate peering (owner: maria.net), ashley to root cause the CPU hotloop and clean up autoscaler (owner: ashley.prod), ben to run post-change latency rollbacks and validate synthetic probes (owner: ben.sre). if p99 stays >600ms after 30m we'll escalate to incident and schedule a postmortem.

maria.net: quick note — collecting tcpdump and flow logs for 5043216000-5043217600 window and uploading to /mnt/sre/artifacts/eu-routing-5043216789.tar.gz.

ben.sre: thanks — set a follow-up check in 20m. adding this thread to the incident tracker if regression reappears. :thumbsup:
